newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retailer files for court protection - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan retailer files for court protection - report.

text.p: Leading Japanese women's wear retailer Suzuya has applied for court mediation with creditors with debts totalling 52.67 billion yen, credit research company Teikoku Databank said in a statement on Monday.

The company, established in 1971, filed the application with the Tokyo District Court on Monday after failing to win necessary support for its new restructuring plans earlier this month from other firms, the private research company reported.

It said the privately held company, which operates women's clothing chains and also runs a shopping mall in the fashionable Aoyama district of Tokyo, had suffered from stagnant domestic sales and hefty interest payments on its borrowings.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment on Teikoku Databank's report. An official at the Tokyo District Court declined to confirm or deny the report.
The 52.67 billion yen debt includes 10 billion yen worth of debts of group companies which were guaranteed by Suzuya, Teikoku said.
Creditor mediation is a process under which troubled entities can avoid going bankrupt and seek to continue in business under supervision.
